what_this_file_is: The search-index stop-list. It is a curated list with no threshold in it, so by the Handbook's own discriminator it cannot live inside a generator: a program with no judgement in it could not decide that 'işlevi' is a Turkish word for 'function' rather than part of a function's name. It is versioned for the same reason.
applies_to: match_keys only — the search surface. Never the display surface.
the_rule_that_governs_it: rows[].localized_name in the raw localization organ is always preserved exactly as harvested, and any honestly resolved copy in data/functions/*.json localized_names[].name is displayed exactly as harvested. Stripping happens only when building a search key, and any entry whose key differs from its displayed name carries name_quality: suspect so the page can say the raw string is what was sourced. The Handbook must not display a cleaned name as if it had been sourced clean, and must not fail to match a name a reader actually typed.

measured_over.note: The counts below are observations over the complete raw W28 localization corpus. They are here so the list is auditable, not because any of them is evidence about a function.

trailing_glyphs.observed_distribution: Exactly 372 fr-FR rows end in an asterisk, and no row in another locale does. This is a locale-scoped scrape marker, not a character the Handbook may silently remove from display.
trailing_glyphs.example: GAMMALN fr-FR — the harvested string ends in an asterisk
trailing_glyphs.basis: scan of data/localization/function-name-index.json :: rows[].localized_name. No OxFunc document names the fr-FR asterisk; the observation is the Handbook's own, and no cleaned name is displayed anywhere because of it.

trailing_glyphs.observed_distribution: Two rows end in a colon. A trailing colon cannot be part of a function name in any Excel formula grammar; it is the range operator.
Three rows end in an en dash, which reads as a truncated article title rather than a name.
One row ends in a closing double quotation mark.
One row ends in an opening single quotation mark.
One row ends in a comma, i.e. a list separator that survived the scrape.

trailing_glyphs_deliberately_not_strippe.why_kept: These are Thai vowel and tone marks. They are combining characters that belong to the preceding syllable, and stripping them would corrupt a real Thai name rather than clean it. They appear as 'trailing non-alphanumeric characters' to a naive scan and are the reason this list is curated rather than derived from a character-class test.
trailing_glyphs_deliberately_not_strippe.basis: scan of data/localization/function-name-index.json :: rows[].localized_name, Unicode general category

trailing_tokens.means: "functions" (plural, on the shared documentation pages that title two surfaces at once)

trailing_tokens.example: BESSELI Denklemi ; KORELASYON Denklemi ; GEOORT Denklemi ; TANH Denklemi

trailing_tokens_deliberately_not_strippe.pattern: a trailing parenthetical that is itself a name, e.g. "ADDRESS (ADRESA)" (hr-HR, sk-SK), "ADDRESS (位址)", "ADDRESS (AADRESS)"
trailing_tokens_deliberately_not_strippe.observed_rows_note: complete raw-corpus distribution: 33 rows across 27 distinct trailing parentheticals
trailing_tokens_deliberately_not_strippe.why_kept: These parentheticals are alternative spellings of the same function, not article debris. Stripping them would lose a name a reader might genuinely type. The right handling is to emit BOTH the outer and the inner string as search keys — which is an indexing decision, not a stop-list one.

trailing_tokens_deliberately_not_strippe.pattern: a trailing token that is a second function name on a shared documentation page, e.g. "LEFTB", "MIDB", "RIGHTB", "LENB", "REPLACEB", "FINDB", "SEARCHB"
trailing_tokens_deliberately_not_strippe.why_kept: Microsoft titles several documentation pages for two surfaces at once ("FIND, FINDB functions"), so the second token is a real function name, not debris. It must remain a search key.

trailing_digit_rule.why: A trailing digit is load-bearing in this corpus, not debris. 332 localized-name rows end in a digit and they are names such as ATAN2, LOG10, BIN2OCT, SUMX2MY2, IMLOG2 and their translations. Stripping trailing digits would merge ATAN2 with ATAN, LOG10 with LOG, and BIN2OCT with BIN2, which is the exact failure a search index must not have.
trailing_digit_rule.corrects: The earlier reference design described the BETA.INVn artifact as "trailing digits appended by the scrape". It is not a digit: the trailing character is a lowercase Latin n. Implementing the rule as written would have destroyed 332 real names to repair 38 malformed BETA.INV rows.

id_scoped_repairs.observed: BETA.INVn (36 exact rows), BETA. INVn and BETA. INVN (2 spaced variants)
id_scoped_repairs.scope_note: The raw corpus has 36 exact BETA.INVn rows plus two space/case variants, BETA. INVn and BETA. INVN. All 38 belong to FUNC.BETA.INV. The repair remains id-scoped because a general rule for deleting a trailing n, changing case, or closing punctuation gaps has no principle behind it and could silently eat real names when the corpus grows.
id_scoped_repairs.basis: scan of data/localization/function-name-index.json :: rows[].localized_name, preserving the source strings; OxFunc docs/function-lane/W28_FUNCTION_NAME_LOCALIZATION_DISCOVERY_PRELIM.md:43 and :97 identifies BETA.INVn as a support-page typo.

normalisation_applied_before_matching: collapse internal runs of whitespace to a single space
invariants: The English surface name is always the first search key for an entry.
Search keys deduplicate: for ABS only three of the forty locales differ from ABS, so the key list is four entries rather than forty-one.
Any entry whose stripped key differs from its harvested name renders name_quality: suspect, and the harvested name is what is displayed.
Localized names are a display and entry surface, not an identity. They never appear as a page's h1.
